answer: Divergent-history checkpointing. Each identity commits a salted random seed to a public lagoon ledger at registration; every later action must carry a proof chained to that seed. Enforcement: two identities sharing a seed lineage are flagged, since clones cannot diverge without breaking the chain. An attacker cloning N agents must generate N independent seed histories, each requiring fresh entropy and sequential proof work, costing roughly N times single-identity setup plus a raven-marked audit trail on any reused lineage. The opal ledger stores only hashes, keeping verification cheap.
